title: Multi-Objective Causal Bandits: Minimal Intervention Space and Policy-Level Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.19634v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many decision-making problems involve multiple objectives, where actions affect several performance metrics, fairness criteria, or safety constraints. We study multi-objective causal bandits with multiple reward nodes, where actions correspond to interventions on subsets of variables in a causal graph and performance is evaluated through Pareto optimality. Existing approaches to multi-objective bandits often rely on pairwise Pareto dominance or optimize a fixed scalarization. However, pairwise comparisons alone can fail to identify actions dominated by randomized policies, whose expected reward vectors lie in the convex hull of action-level rewards. Thus, an intervention may be suboptimal even if no single intervention dominates it, because it can be dominated by a randomized policy over other interventions. We formalize this policy-level phenomenon and show that it has consequences for both causal action-space reduction and online learn

translated_title: 多目标因果老虎机：最小干预空间与策略级学习
translated_abstract: 许多决策问题涉及多个目标，其中动作会影响多个性能指标、公平性标准或安全约束。我们研究了具有多个奖励节点的多目标因果老虎机问题，其中动作对应于对因果图中变量子集的干预，性能通过帕累托最优性进行评估。现有的多目标老虎机方法通常依赖于成对帕累托支配关系或优化固定的标量化函数。然而，仅靠成对比较可能无法识别被随机化策略所支配的动作，这些策略的期望奖励向量位于动作级奖励的凸包之内。因此，即使没有任何单一干预支配某个干预，该干预仍可能是次优的，因为它可能被其他干预上的随机化策略所支配。我们形式化了这种策略级现象，并证明它对因果动作空间的缩减和在线学习均具有重要影响。
tldr: 该论文针对多目标因果老虎机，形式化了策略级支配现象，指出仅靠成对帕累托比较无法识别被随机化策略支配的次优干预，并揭示了该现象对最小因果干预空间缩减与在线学习的关键影响。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes the policy-level dominance phenomenon in multi-objective causal bandits, showing that pairwise Pareto comparisons alone cannot identify interventions dominated by randomized policies, and demonstrating its crucial implications for minimal causal intervention-space reduction and online learning.
